primary_article.title: Systematic interrogation of drug sensitivities in melanoma reveals potent synergistic and antagonistic drug combinations with translational potential.

Sec3.title: Cell lines and culturing of cells
Sec3.text: Cell lines and culturing of cellsThe melanoma cell lines used in this study were provided by the Department of Tumor Biology, Institute for Cancer Research, Oslo University Hospital, Oslo, Norway. Cell line information is described in Supplementary Data 1. Mutational status of the cell lines was derived from Cellosaurus29 or from internal analysis: HM1930, Melmet1, and Melmet531, MM382, and MM38832. The cell and drug screening work was covered by Regional Ethics Committee approval REK 2015/1012.All cell lines were grown at 37 °C, 5% CO2, 95% humidity, and regularly tested for mycoplasma infection (LT07-705, Lonza).All the cell lines, except MM382 and MM388 (as they are newly established from melanoma lymph node metastases after informed consent32 under a project approved by the Regional Committee for Medical Research Ethics of South-East Norway, approval number 2014/2208, 2015/2434, see Supplementary Data 1), were authenticated by the provider parties in the genotyping core facility at the Oslo University Hospital, Oslo, Norway using the following protocol as stated in the reports:DNA from 10⁶ to 10⁷ cells was extracted using the Qiagen MagAttract DNA Mini M48 Kit by an automated procedure on the BioRobot M48. The PowerPlex 16 kit (Promega, Nerliens Meszansky) was used to amplify the thirteen core CODIS short tandem repeat (STR) loci plus Penta E, Penta D, and the gender-determining locus, amelogenin. Alleles were determined by capillary electrophoresis on a MegaBACE 1000, followed by data analysis with the software GeneMarker HID. Appropriate positive and negative controls were used throughout the analysis.Additionally, the cell lines A375, MeWo, Skmel28, and WM1366 were authenticated a second time by Eurofins Genomics using this protocol, as stated in the reports. In brief, DNA isolation was carried out from cell pellets. Genetic characteristics were determined by PCR-single-locus-technology. 16 independent PCR-systems D8S1179, D21S11, D7S820, CSF1PO, D3S1358, TH01, D13S317, D16S539, D2S1338, AMEL, D5S818, FGA, D19S433, vWA, TPOX and D18S51 were investigated. In parallel, positive and negative controls were carried out, yielding correct results.The cell lines were cultured in RPMI 1640 GlutaMAX medium (61870044, Gibco) supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS) (F7524, Sigma-Aldrich) and 1% penicillin/streptomycin (15276355, Gibco) except for Hermes 3C and Hermes 4C, which were cultured in 254 medium (M254500, Gibco) supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS) (F7524, Sigma-Aldrich), 1% penicillin/streptomycin (15276355, Gibco), 200 nM phorbol-12-myristate-13-acetate (TPA), (P8139, Sigma-Aldrich), 200 pM (Hermes 3C) and 2 pM (Hermes 4C) cholera toxin (C8052, Sigma-Aldrich), 10 ng/ml human stem cell factor (hSCF) (15319100, Invitrogen) and 10 nM endothelin (EDN1) (E7764, Sigma-Aldrich)33

Sec7.title: Statistics and reproducibility
Sec7.text: Statistics and reproducibilityStatistical significance was tested using Welch’s two-sided Student’s t-test unless stated otherwise. For mouse experiments, statistical analysis was performed as follows. Tumor growth was modeled as a function of time using a linear mixed effects model, taking log tumor volume as the response and accounting for repeated measurements. For fixed effects, we included time, treatment group (untreated, rabusertib, cytarabine, combination), and their interaction, taking as baseline the untreated group. Random intercepts were included to account for the nested structure of the experiment—tumor site within animal. Model fit was evaluated via residual plots stratified by group and Q-Q-plots, with no substantial deviations observed. P-values for the fixed effects were obtained via Satterthwaite’s approximation as implemented in the R package “lmerTest” (version 3.1-3); analysis was conducted in R (version 4.4.3, 2025-02-28).To assess reproducibility of the drug screening results across the dataset, we run three experimental replicates of the same cell line, MeWo, and we analyzed all 1830 drug combinations from the MeWo dataset using the bayesynergy R package. For each replicate, we extracted the posterior mean response from the Bayesian model. Pairwise reproducibility between replicates was quantified using Pearson’s correlation coefficient, computed on the posterior mean responses across all combinations. In the Live-cell microscopy experiments in Figs. 4B and 5D, E the p-values are not adjusted for multiple comparisons and only tests the difference of endpoints.

Sec8.title: Live-cell microscopy experiments
Sec8.text: Live-cell microscopy experimentsLive-cell imaging experiments were conducted in an Incucyte® S3 instrument (Sartorius). Cell death was assessed using Incucyte® Cytotox Green Dye (4633, Sartorius) according to the manufacturer’s instructions. Briefly, cells were seeded at the appropriate density in black-walled, clear-bottom 96-well plates (353219 Falcon, Corning) and incubated overnight (16–24 h) to allow attachment. The day of the experiment drug solutions were prepared in fresh medium containing Incucyte® Cytotox Green Dye and dispensed manually into a 96-well plate according to a predefined treatment layout. For each biological replicate, we included three technical replicates per treatment, except for cytarabine single-drug treatments in Fig. 5D and Supplementary Fig. S6B, where there was only sufficient space on the multiwell plates for two technical replicates.At time zero, after cell attachment for 16–24 h, the cell plate was scanned with the Incucyte® S3 (Sartorius), the medium removed, and the medium containing the drugs added using a PLATEMASTER® (Gilson), enabling simultaneous administration of all treatments. The plate was returned into the Incucyte® S3 and scanned every 3 h. For sequential treatment experiments, following the 24 h scan, the plate was removed, washed twice with fresh medium, and new treatments were added using the PLATEMASTER®. The plate was then returned into the Incucyte® S3 for continued imaging until the 48 h timepoint. Image analysis and quantification were conducted using the Incucyte® analysis software.

Sec9.title: Flow cytometry
Sec9.text: Flow cytometryFor DNA profiles and γH2Ax analysis, we run three independent experiments in different days. Cells were fixed in ice-cold 70% ethanol and stained with mouse anti-phospho-H2Ax (Ser139) at 1:500 (05-636, Millipore; Clone JBW301 Lot: 4156777), followed by Alexa Fluor 488 donkey anti-mouse (A21202, Invitrogen, Lot: 2563848) or Alexa Fluor 647 goat anti-mouse (A-21235, Invitrogen, Lot 1786359) secondary antibodies at 1:1000, and the DNA stain Hoechst 33258 (1.5 μg/ml) or FxCycle Far Red (200 nM FxCycle and 0.1 mg/ml RNase A) (F10348, Invitrogen). Flow cytometry analysis was performed on a LSRII flow cytometer (BD Biosciences) and using FlowJo software version 10.
